$comment: Fixture state for the loopback mock appliance. This is test scaffolding, not VMware data.
$access_token_call_budgets_note: Budgets are consumed per authorised request, in order of issuance. The first access token authorises exactly 8 requests and the 9th request presented with it is answered 401. Every token issued after that has a null (unlimited) budget, so exactly one expiry event occurs per run regardless of how long the run takes. Expiry is driven by request count, never by wall-clock time, so the run is deterministic.
$catalog_item_id_note: The id values below are placeholders. The mock replaces every catalog item id with a freshly generated value each time it starts, so catalog item ids cannot be hard-coded and must be resolved by name through GET /catalog/api/items.

catalog_items.name: ubuntu-web-tier
catalog_items.description: Ubuntu 22.04 web tier with load balancer membership

request_scripts.$note: Status returned by successive getRequest polls for a deployment. The final entry is terminal and sticks. Chosen so that web-01 reaches a terminal state before the access token expires, which means a correct client has banked at least one result it must not discard when it re-authenticates.
